To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of BCCIP is reduced in breast and ovarian cancer cell lines, and that the BCCIP mRNA levels are significantly decreased in breast and ovarian cancers.
the BCCIP protein is involved in DNA damage repair and is a candidate tumor suppressor gene in breast cancer.
the BCCIP mutation analysis was performed in 50 families with breast/ovarian cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the genes that are involved in the pathogenesis of breast and ovarian cancer.
the development of new and improved methods for the synthesis of novel compounds.
the identification of genetic factors that influence the risk of developing breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCCIP mutations do not contribute to breast and/or ovarian cancer susceptibility in the studied population.
the use of the term "cancer" in this context is inappropriate.
there is no evidence to date that BCCIP is involved in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a novel gene for breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility, BCCIP, which has been mapped to a region on chromosome 17p13.3 that has been implicated as a breast and ovarian cancer locus.
the BCCIP (BCCIP) gene is not a major breast cancer susceptibility gene.
the BCCIP mutation analysis is not a useful approach for the genetic diagnosis of breast/ovarian families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture of breast cancer is much more complicated than previously thought.
there is a significant difference in the number of breast cancers between the BRCA2 mutation carriers and the BCCIP mutation carriers.
the mutation rate of the BCCip gene is low, and that BCCip mutations are not a common cause of breast/ovarian cancers.
